correctness.rationale: The statement is mathematically correct. Cintioli Definition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3 give for every real Y, H(Y)≡_T Y’ when omega_1^Y=omega_1^CK and H(Y)≡_T O^Y otherwise, and always Y<_T H(Y). The standard relative Church–Kleene fact omega_1^{Y’}=omega_1^Y preserves the low regime under jumps. The hyperjump computes its input, so the high regime is monotone and remains high. Induction then gives H^n(X)≡_T X^(n) or Q_n(X) for all finite n and strict growth. No limit ordinal claim; induction correctly uses Turing degree invariance of relativized O.

originality.rationale: FAIL as independently novel mathematics. The full claimed finite iteration dichotomy follows immediately by reapplying the published Cintioli one-step theorem, already quantified for every real, using standard jump preservation and oracle monotonicity. This is a direct induction/corollary of a stronger existing theorem even though the source paper does not explicitly use the word iteration. Neither renaming H^n nor stating both cases for all finite n establishes a new independent result.
